acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

data.reason: Angela, the COO, signed with Adyen after we never showed a till return or a store rollout plan. Tom thought Raj decided and that winning online mattered, but stores decided it.

trigger.action: Lead with returning an online order at the store till.
trigger.why: Angela watched a holiday returns queue because stores couldn't see online orders.
trigger.quote: The store couldn't see the online order

decider.action: Tell store-side leaders who answers when tills fail, not only payments.
decider.why: Angela signed with Adyen, and our answer on installs was to 'bring in a partner'.
decider.quote: I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.

competitor.action: Answer store rollout questions: installs, wifi drops, Saturday till outages.
competitor.why: Per Raj, secondhand, Adyen brought people who'd done store rollouts. Afterward most questions were about stores.
competitor.quote: Raj forwarded me a list of 14 questions and 11 of them were about stores.

message.action: Replace 'the line has disappeared' with a step-by-step till return.
message.why: Bev, head of store operations, dismissed our unified commerce slide and asked how a return works.

proof.action: Add a retailer story with rollout dates, installs and old tills.
proof.why: Angela wanted to call the retailer in our case study, and we couldn't arrange it in time.

words.action: Say 'the tills', not 'point of sale' or 'unified commerce'.
words.why: Bev used this phrase every time, while we kept saying 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale'.
words.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
